example_statement: In 2022, twice as many males as females exceeded the risky drinking guideline in Queensland (48.9% for males and 24.5% for females)
In 2022–23, standardised hospitalisation rates were 25.5% higher in remote areas compared to major cities
In 2022–23, standardised hospitalisation rates were 18.9% higher in the most disadvantaged compared to the most advantaged areas
The prevalence of risky drinking in the Queensland adult population decreased by 5.3% from 2012 to 2022
From 2002–03 to 2022–23, standardised hospitalisation rates increased 51.5% in adults
Hospitalisations for the combined group of seven chronic diseases decreased by 18.0% from 2015–16 to 2022–23
In 2022–2023, more than 1-in-10 (10.5%) Queensland high school students had smoked tobacco in the previous 12 months
In 2022–23, potentially preventable hospitalisations account for 6.4% of all hospitalisations
The proportion of Queensland adult males who smoked daily has decreased by 53.4% from 2002 to 2024
